subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the rank of the matrix with rows (1, 4, −1), (2, 3, 0) and (0, 1, 2).

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the rank of this matrix.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Test the 3×3 determinant
steps.margin_note: First mark. The matrix is 3×3, so the rank cannot be more than 3. Start at that top size and expand the whole determinant.
steps.memory_tip: Rank is at most the smaller of the row count and the column count — here that is 3.

recall.must_convey: That the whole 3×3 determinant is the largest minor, and that expanding it gives −12.
accept: the matrix is three by three so expand the full determinant first
take the determinant of the whole matrix, it comes to minus twelve
the largest minor is the three by three determinant and it is minus twelve
moda full determinant expand cheste minus twelve vasthundi
expand along the first row and get six minus sixteen minus two

steps.why: Rank is the order of the largest non-zero minor. The largest minor a 3×3 matrix has is the whole determinant, so that is the first thing to test.
common_mistakes: Expanding along a row and losing the + − + sign pattern.
Reading a rank off the original matrix with no test at all.

steps.label: State the rank
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A non-zero minor of order 3 exists, and a 3×3 matrix has no minor of order 4, so 3 is the largest order possible.
steps.memory_tip: A non-zero 3×3 determinant settles it at once — the rank is the full 3.
lines: |A| = −12 ≠ 0, so a minor of order 3 is
non-zero. A 3×3 matrix has no minor of
order 4, so 3 is the largest order.

recall.must_convey: That a non-zero determinant of order 3 fixes the rank at 3, with no larger minor available.
accept: the determinant is not zero so the rank is three
minus twelve is not zero, so a three order minor is non zero and the rank is three
there is no order four minor here so three is the largest and the rank is three
determinant zero kaadu kabatti rank three

steps.why: One non-zero minor of order 3 is enough. Nothing larger exists inside a 3×3 matrix, so no further checking is possible or needed.
common_mistakes: Going on to test 2×2 minors when the 3×3 one is already non-zero.
Writing the value −12 as the rank.
